course_description:
The course is part of a suite of Literacy and English courses in the Bachelor of Education (Primary) degree. It aims to develop preservice teachers’ knowledge and understanding of the essential elements of reading that should be taught in early, middle, and upper primary school contexts, including phonological awareness, phonics, comprehension, vocabulary, and fluency. Preservice teachers will apply this knowledge through the analysis and synthesis of contemporary theories of reading. The course also aims to develop students’ understanding of and skills in planning for, teaching, and assessing reading lessons. Application of knowledge and skills will be demonstrated through the completion of a sequence of quizzes and the design of early and upper primary reading lesson and assessment plans. The course also teaches important connections between reading, oral language, and spelling, and emphasises how to support the reading development of all students.

This course provides preservice teachers with a comprehensive introduction to early reading theory, development, and pedagogy. The course is one of four within the Bachelor of Education (Primary) program that focuses on the teaching and learning of English in the primary years. In this course, preservice teachers will develop specialised knowledge of contemporary early reading theories related to the essential elements of reading, including oral language, phonological awareness, phonics, comprehension, vocabulary, and fluency; develop a repertoire of pedagogical strategies to teach and assess all essential elements of reading; analyse and evaluate key concepts related to common reading difficulties experienced by beginning readers, particularly dyslexia, specific comprehension difficulties, and mixed reading difficulties; develop advanced and integrated understanding of connections between reading and other complex literate practices, particularly oral language (speaking and listening) and spelling. Key reading theories that underpin the course include the simple view of reading, Scarborough's reading rope, the dual route model, Rosenshine's principles of explicit instruction, and response to intervention. Preservice teachers will investigate and make judgements about aspects of the Australian Curriculum: English to design high-quality, challenging, research-based teaching and learning activities focused on early and upper primary reading. Preservice teachers will also explore current and contemporary approaches and research related to the assessment of students’ reading capabilities. Strategies and resources utilised throughout EDUC2720 are designed to enable you to demonstrate attainment of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at the graduate level. Specifically, the course's teaching and learning activities and assessment tasks target the following standards: 1.2, 2.1, 2.3, 2.5, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 4.2, 5.1, 5.4

assessment_details.task_description: This task requires you to complete a sequence of three quizzes, drawing on your developing understanding of the essential elements of reading instruction. Quiz 1 focuses on phonological awareness, Quiz 2 focuses on fluency, and Quiz 3 focuses on vocabulary (CC 2.4.1: Practised). The quizzes are completed in your scheduled tutorials for Week 4 (Quiz 1), Week 6 (Quiz 2), and Week 8 (Quiz 3). The quizzes are paper based and must be answered using a standard pen or pencil. Quiz papers are provided at the start of each quiz, but you must bring your own pen/pencil. You may not use any other resources/devices to complete these quizzes (e.g., supporting materials, computers, phones, smartwatches, etc.). Marking Quiz questions are a mix of short and long responses. Marks are earned through demonstrating your depth of understanding for each of the quiz topics. Each quiz in the sequence is marked out of 7, and is weighted at 15%, for a combined total of 45% weighting of the course. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Planning early and upper primary reading lessons
assessment_details.weight: 55% This assignment is considered the equivalent of a 2,500-word essay
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment task will develop your knowledge of how to teach and assess reading, with a focus on early and upper primary reading. It is split into two parts. Part 1: Lesson and assessment plans You are required to plan two standalone reading lessons, with a phonics lesson designed for an early primary context (i.e., Prep, Year 1, or Year 2) and a comprehension lesson designed for an upper primary context (i.e., Year 5 or 6). Each lesson will be supported by your use of an appropriate mentor text. Select ONE reading-related Content Description per lesson from a set of options on Blackboard that could be taught using your selected mentor texts. Each Content Description will be linked to a given year level in the Australian Curriculum: English . The Content Description you select will determine the year levels for your planning. Each lesson must include: Achievable yet challenging learning goals for students, communicated in student-friendly language through learning intention(s) and success criteria. A description of how you would teach the essential element of reading in the genre of a procedural text that could be picked up and used by other teachers. Examples of teacher talk, think-alouds, and modelling with one or several mentor texts. An indication of how student learning would be assessed (please detail how you would meaningfully integrate assessment opportunities into your learning experiences). Part 2: Theoretical rationale Write a theoretical rationale to justify the choices made in your lesson and assessment plans. Your theoretical rationale should explain: How you drew on relevant curriculum documents and scholarly literature when planning each part of your lessons. How and why you incorporated differentiated teaching strategies to cater for students with varying abilities and characteristics. Your use of appropriate resources to teach and assess reading (e.g., mentor texts, effective use of Information and Communication Technology). This assignment is considered the equivalent of a 2500-word essay . Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Week 1 Overview and history of reading instruction; Contemporary theories of early reading This lecture and tutorial explore the history of reading instruction, from the ABC method, to phonics, the look-say approach, whole language, balanced literacy, and arriving in the present with a science of reading-informed approach. Preservice teachers also learn about key reading theories underpinning the course, including the simple view of reading, Scarborough's reading rope, and the dual route model.

Week 2 Oral language and reading This week focuses on oral language. Preservice teachers learn about how oral language skills develop, the components of oral language, the relationship between oral language and reading, and how primary teachers foster these skills in classrooms (CC 2.4.1: Taught, Practised).

Week 3 Phonological awareness; Concepts of print; Alphabet knowledge This lecture and tutorial introduce three important aspects of early reading: phonological awareness, alphabet knowledge, and concepts about print. This lays groundwork for the next lecture and tutorial on phonics (CC 2.4.1: Taught, Practised).

Week 4 Phonics Preservice teachers learn how to help children develop their word recognition skills, bringing together their knowledge of decoding and reading high-frequency words. Everyone has undoubtedly heard about phonics before, and this week, preservice teachers learn to teach phonics systematically, explicitly, and synthetically (CC 2.4.1: Taught, Practised).

Week 5 Fluency This week focuses on fluency, which acts as a critical bridge between word recognition processes and comprehension processes. Preservice teachers learn about the aspects of fluency that allow readers to read accurately, quickly, and with great expression, clarity, and phrasing. In the lecture, preservice teachers will be taught about the components of reading fluency, the Australian Curriculum: English content descriptions and achievement standards related to fluency, and are introduced to the multidimensional fluency rubric (Rasinski & Young, 2022) as one of several strategies that can be used to summatively assess reading fluency (CC 2.3.3: Taught). In the tutorial, they will listen to a recording of a child reading and summatively assess their reading fluency using the multidimensional fluency rubric, considering the child’s expression and volume, phrasing, smoothness, and pace (CC 2.3.3: Practised).

Week 8 Comprehension strategies This week focuses on several comprehension strategies teachers can teach to enhance the mental models their students build when they are reading. This helps preservice teachers to understand the aspects that make up the language and reading comprehension aspects of the simple view of reading and Scarborough's reading rope. This content once again highlights the complexity of reading instruction in contemporary primary school classrooms (CC 2.4.1: Taught, Practised).

Week 6 Language comprehension and reading comprehension; Comprehending components Comprehending (or understanding) is the reason people read. This week, preservice teachers will learn about several components of comprehension, including inference, background knowledge, knowledge of grammar structures, knowledge of text structures, and comprehension monitoring, which come together to allow readers to build a strong mental model of the texts they are reading. The lecture explains research showing student understanding, engagement, and academic performance are improved by the explicit comprehension instruction in the context of discipline-specific content (CC 2.4.2: Taught). During the lecture, preservice teachers will work with a partner to select from a range of ‘Core Knowledge’ readers on History and Geography or Science topics, become familiar with the content noting points that were not part of their background knowledge, and consider how they might draw on the Core Knowledge materials to explicitly teach reading comprehension and writing in these disciplines (CC 2.4.2: Practised).

Week 7 Vocabulary This week focuses on vocabulary, with particular emphasis paid to vocabulary depth, breadth, and access. The lecture and tutorial explore three tiers of words and explain why focusing on Tier 2 words is particularly important in the direct teaching of vocabulary. The lecture teaches how to explicitly deliver this important element of reading instruction through discipline specific curriculum areas (CC 2.4.3: Taught), with opportunities for preservice teachers to practice developing and delivering reading instruction resources for this purpose (CC 2.4.3: Practised).

Week 9 Explicit reading instruction; Supporting all readers This week focuses on how teachers can teach and assess reading using an explicit approach named the gradual release of responsibility. Video clips are shared of several assessment methods mentioned in previous weeks. Preservice teachers will learn about creating learning intentions and success criteria, how to break up learning tasks into manageable chunks (CC 2.2.2: Taught), how these chunks can be logically sequenced (CC 2.2.3: Taught), and how to scaffold student learning (CC 2.2.4: Taught). Following this, the lecture explores different ways to support students who struggle with the elements of reading. In the tutorial, preservice teachers will engage in a comparative judgement task where they compare and discuss key features of explicit phonics instruction (CC 2.2.4 – practised). They will review and revise comprehension lessons using the principles of explicit instruction (CC 2.2.2, 2.2.3: Practised). Learning outcomes: L02, L03

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 10 To Week 11 (05 Oct - 18 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Weeks 10 and 11 In Weeks 10 and 11, EDUC7620 preservice teachers in the 'Standard' Master of Teaching (Primary) Program will be on their school professional experience placements. Since EDUC2720 is jointly taught with EDUC7620, this means no lectures or tutorials will be held in Weeks 10 or 11 for either cohort.

Week 12 Links between reading and spelling This week focuses on how teachers can teach and assess spelling. Preservice teachers learn about the four spelling competencies and various methods of teaching and assessing spelling in classrooms, as well as connections with how teachers teach phonics and decoding (spelling involves encoding). Learning outcomes: L02, L03

Week 13 Bringing together the essential elements of reading; Course reflection This last week teaches preservice teachers how the strategies and topics of reading come together in primary classrooms. Learning outcomes: L02, L03
